_comment: Nether pit density. The cavernous noise (minecraft:nether/base_3d_noise) contributes ACROSS the whole pit Y range, no Y-band masks — the previous version masked noise to a thin Y=-30..10 slice, and the noise router's vertical interpolation chopped that slice into the visible horizontal-banded 'mesh' pattern. With noise contributing throughout, the pit interior is organic 3D nether terrain (caves, pockets, walls) instead of a layered slice. Solid_floor shapes the bottom (below Y=-40), air_cap forces air above Y=40 — gives a roughly 90-block-tall pit with cavernous nether terrain inside.

argument1._comment: Solid floor below Y=-50. Ramps to 0 at Y=-40 so the bottom of the pit has lots of solid netherrack — a place to land.

Air cap above Y=40 — ramps to -30 by Y=60 so anything above the pit is decisively air. Magnitude high enough that the noise router's quart-cell interpolation at the Voronoi rim doesn't grow a thick netherrack lip.

argument2._comment: nether/base_3d_noise contributing density everywhere (no Y-band mask). Magnitude ~±1. In the pit interior Y=-40..40 where solid_floor and air_cap are both near 0, the noise alone drives density: positive samples are netherrack walls/pillars, negative samples are caves/air pockets. Vanilla nether biome features (lake_lava) fill the air pockets with lava as the world generates.
